headline: Apple Sends Spyware Attack Alerts to Users in 110 Countries
summary: Apple is now sending push notifications directly to iPhones warning users of potential mercenary spyware attacks, urging immediate action to protect devices.
details: Apple has begun sending a new wave of threat notifications to customers suspected of being targeted by sophisticated spyware. These alerts, sent to users in 110 countries, warn of potential attacks on iPhones, iPads, and Macs, typically employed by state-sponsored actors.

The tech giant has updated its user experience to deliver these warnings directly on the iPhone lock screen via push notifications. The alert reads: “Apple detected a mercenary spyware attack targeted at your iPhone. There are actions you can take now to protect your data and device.”

Beyond lock screen alerts, Apple also notifies users via email and when they log into their Apple ID. This enhanced communication aims to make it easier for recipients to access critical information and understand the necessary steps to secure their devices.

Upon receiving a notification, users are advised to enable Lockdown Mode, a security feature designed to significantly hinder spyware attacks. Apple states it has not yet encountered a successful device hack when Lockdown Mode was active.

While spyware attacks are generally rare, their increasing prevalence has led to their misuse by governments against critics and civil society members. These notifications are crucial for uncovering such abuses, as highlighted by past investigations that revealed widespread spyware deployment.

headline: Microsoft removes Mico avatar from Copilot voice mode
summary: The emotive yellow blob, once pitched as Copilot's identity, is being moved to a new platform.
details: Microsoft has announced that its Mico avatar will no longer be featured in Copilot's voice mode. The company stated that Mico will be moved to its Learn Live platform, where it will have "more to react to."

Mico was launched in October last year, with Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman describing it as a way to give the chatbot an "identity." The avatar was designed to react in real-time to user input with facial expressions and animations.

This move marks the retirement of another virtual assistant from Microsoft, joining the ranks of Clippy, Cortana, and Rover. Microsoft indicated that the learnings from Mico's use in Copilot are "shaping Copilot going forward."

The removal of Mico is part of Microsoft's broader strategy to merge its Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot applications. This change follows a recent AI leadership reshuffling that placed Jacob Andreou in charge of Copilot.
